digest.component_or_area: agent subprocess lifecycle management and process monitoring
propositions: Subagents spawn unbounded CPU saturation workers (python -c 'while True: pass') to investigate timing-dependent failures, but these processes are never reaped when the harness exits, becoming PPID-1 orphans that run indefinitely

On the affected host, 38 such orphaned workers accumulated ~138,000 CPU-seconds combined over four days at ~1341% CPU, causing load average 58.49 and preventing application launch until manually killed
No repository-side fixture can prevent recurrence because the workers are ad-hoc python -c invocations with no code footprint; the defect is a guidance and detection gap

Agent guidance must mandate bounding all background processes at spawn time (e.g. timeout 120) and process-group teardown (trap 'kill 0' EXIT INT TERM), with explicit prohibition on PPID-1 orphans and operator notes for reclamation

A detection check must identify compute processes with PPID 1 and CPU time exceeding 3600 seconds (default), excluding system-owned executables that legitimately have PPID 1 on macOS, with injectable process-inspection seam for testability
